about: Studies like this one (REVIEW_ISSUES R06e, R37). Every PSI related-investigation link is included in both directions; other suggestions written with Claude Code. basis: psi_link (PSI lists the link), hardware (same flight hardware family), fuel (same fuel class), role (shared fire-safety role), finding (a checked finding covers both). Each basis is checked against the data by pipeline/ai_build.mjs.

PSI-25.reason: BASS-II is the follow-on to BASS: same glovebox flow duct and solid fuels, with oxygen now lowered and recorded.
SAFFIRE-II burned solid samples in a Cygnus vehicle and compared them with burns in normal gravity.
BRE emulates burning solids with a gas burner and reports burning at elevated oxygen, which BASS-II did not reach.

PSI-26.reason: BASS-II reflew the BASS hardware with oxygen lowered and recorded in its table.
SAFFIRE-I burned the same cotton-fiberglass fabric (SIBAL) as BASS, but as one large sample in a Cygnus vehicle.
PSI links SPICE to BASS: both used a fan-driven flow duct in the station glovebox.

PSI-98.reason: SAFFIRE-II used the same Cygnus flow unit with nine smaller samples of several materials.
SAFFIRE-III repeated the large cotton-fiberglass burn at a higher airflow.
BASS burned the same cotton-fiberglass fabric at small scale in the station glovebox.

PSI-99.reason: SAFFIRE-I used the same Cygnus flow unit for one large cotton-fiberglass sample.
SAFFIRE-III is the third flight of the same hardware, with a large sample at higher airflow.
BASS-II burned PMMA, also a SAFFIRE-II material, at small scale with oxygen varied.

PSI-100.reason: SAFFIRE-I burned the same large cotton-fiberglass sample at a lower airflow, so the two flights bracket the flow effect.
SAFFIRE-II flew the same hardware with several materials and recorded oxygen, which SAFFIRE-III did not.

PSI-102.reason: SAME-R reflew SAME on the same hardware after the first flight's particle samples came back contaminated.
DAFT checked the P-Trak particle counter in microgravity as a risk-reduction test for SAME.

PSI-101.reason: SAME is the original flight; SAME-R repeated it with broader conditions and a new instrument.
DAFT tested the particle counter used in this family of smoke experiments.

PSI-47.reason: DAFT was the risk-reduction test for SAME's particle counter; SAME then measured smoke from real materials.
SAME-R reflew the smoke measurements with broader conditions.

PSI-69.reason: FLEX-2 extended FLEX on the same droplet apparatus to more fuels and atmospheres.
PSI links CFI to FLEX: the cool flames FLEX discovered became the subject of CFI, on the same droplet apparatus.

PSI-68.reason: FLEX is the first flight of this droplet series and the one with stated suppression findings.
CFI used the same droplet apparatus to study cool flames in more detail.

PSI-39.reason: PSI links CFI to FLEX, where cool flames after hot-flame extinction were first seen.
ACME CFI-G studies cool flames with gas fuels instead of droplets.

PSI-20.reason: ACME Flame Design used the same ACME burner hardware and also reached 40% oxygen.
BASS-II burned real solid fuels, the materials BRE emulates with a gas burner.

PSI-10.reason: ACME CFI-G used the same spherical-flame setup, normal and inverse, to look for cool diffusion flames.
ACME s-Flame studied spherical diffusion flames on the same ACME hardware.

PSI-159.reason: ACME Flame Design used the same spherical-flame setup and atmospheres up to 40% oxygen.
CFI studies cool flames around fuel droplets rather than gas flames.

PSI-21.reason: SLICE studied lifted coflow flames in the glovebox and, per NASA's Guide, is the precursor to CLD Flame.
ACME E-FIELD Flames also used a coflow burner on the same ACME hardware.

PSI-22.reason: PSI links E-FIELD Flames to s-Flame; both are ACME gas-flame studies on the same hardware.
ACME CLD Flame used a coflow burner like the one E-FIELD Flames tested under an electric field.

PSI-23.reason: PSI links s-Flame to E-FIELD Flames; both are ACME gas-flame studies on the same hardware.
ACME Flame Design also studied spherical diffusion flames on the same ACME hardware.

PSI-107.reason: SLICE reused the SPICE flow duct in the glovebox to study lifted flames.
PSI links BASS to SPICE: both used a fan-driven flow duct in the station glovebox.

PSI-106.reason: SPICE is the earlier glovebox experiment whose hardware SLICE reused.
ACME CLD Flame continues SLICE's lifted coflow-flame research on ACME hardware.
